_comment: Canonical train/val/test split for the polybench offline-RL (SFT) and online GRPO-v2 claims. Single source of truth: cite THIS file, not any per-run config. See splits.md for prose.
_split_basis_note: The split is held out BY BENCHMARK (not by sample). A benchmark's rows are entirely in one split. train/val/test are pairwise-disjoint.

offline_sft.content: BOTH single-shot translation AND multi-turn agentic trajectories, mixed. Of 3766 train rows: 465 are single-shot (<=3 messages: system/user/assistant) and 3301 are agentic (>3 messages: the c2hls translate->repair->optimize loop). The split does NOT depend on turn count; it is the same benchmark partition for translation and agentic rows alike.
offline_sft.checkpoint: models/qwen7b_sft_v1 (see models.md) — trained on the train split only

online_grpo_v2.note: GRPO-v2 (kernels_polybench/) trains from the 7B BASE on the SAME train benchmarks, so offline-SFT and online-GRPO-v2 are directly comparable on val/test. Held-out = val + test.

eval_suite.name: polybench-26
eval_suite._relationship: The reported evals run on this 26-benchmark suite, which is NOT identical to the SFT corpus's benchmark set. Read these caveats before quoting eval numbers as 'held-out':
eval_suite._naming_note: The suite uses hyphens for multi-word names (hlsfactory_floyd-warshall, hlsfactory_jacobi-1d, hlsfactory_fdtd-2d, hlsfactory_seidel-2d, hlsfactory_heat-3d); the SFT corpus uses underscores. They denote the same benchmarks.

online_grpo_v1_rodinia.note: The ORIGINAL online-RL (GRPO v1) uses a DIFFERENT benchmark universe entirely: 17 rodinia/ML4Accel tasks in kernels_c2hls/. It has no polybench overlap. Its polybench-26 numbers are fully out-of-domain. Do NOT conflate its split with this file.
